newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond spreads widen again.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond spreads widen again.

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads blew out sharply against other dollar bloc bonds for the second consecutive day as the local market continued to correct its massive rally of the last few weeks.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widened to pre-Federal budget levels after sinking to 120 basis points on Monday, its lowest level in over two years, traders said.
Meanwhile, the Canadian debt market remained a strong performer, outpacing both Australia and a weakened U.S. bond market as it continued to benefit from its current bullish fundamentals.
The five-year part of the Canadian curve was trading below the U.S. for the first time since the 1980's on Monday.
U.S. Treasuries continued to be gripped by fears of a tightening in monetary policy by the Federal Reserve after the recent spate of strong economic data.
The key U.S. 30-year long bond yield hit the 7.0 percent for the first time in four weeks on Monday, before slipping back to 6.97 percent in Tokyo.
